title: IFC task dependencies exist in the schema but are populated only by 4D exporters, and carry no dates
content:
`IfcRelSequence` is a standardised, typed task dependency inside the IFC schema, with predecessor logic (`FINISH_START`, `START_START`, `FINISH_FINISH`, `START_FINISH`) and a `TimeLag`. It is widely assumed to be unused. The sharper rule, measured on one project delivered two ways, is that **design-tool exports carry nothing and 4D-tool exports carry the graph**.

The 48 MB ArchiCAD design model contained no `IfcTask` and no `IfcRelSequence`. The weekly as-planned models of the same building, exported by Synchro's IFC 4D exporter, contained **125 `IfcTask` and 42 `IfcRelSequence`** (41 `FINISH_START`, 1 `START_START`) with real activity names — setting out, pour, prefab stairs, calcium-silicate blockwork.

So the dependency edge is not missing from the industry. It is trapped in 4D exports that nobody queries, which is a materially different problem and a much cheaper one to solve.

Two caveats bound what can be built on it. **0 of 125 tasks carried `IfcTaskTime`**, so scheduled start, finish and duration are absent; the sequence topology travels and the dates do not, and anything date-dependent needs another source. And edges frequently run from an activity to itself by name (`Maatvoering → Maatvoering`), because the exporter emitted per-zone task instances rather than a clean activity network, so deduplication or zone-awareness is required before the graph reads sensibly.
description: A design export held 0 tasks; the Synchro 4D export of the same project held 125 IfcTask and 42 IfcRelSequence edges, but 0 of 125 carried IfcTaskTime. Topology travels, dates do not.
